_note: Data-claim manifest — the single source of truth for the book's governed data cross-references. One entry per grounded datum. A `[data: <slug>]` marker in the prose resolves against this file to a footnote-style cross-ref into the chapter that reports the number (fail-loud on an unknown slug, like an unknown {{token}}). Fields: `source` = the chapter slug (a book/<slug>.html page) that reports the datum; `anchor` = the {#heading-id} on that chapter's reporting section ("" until the render lands); `holds` = the load-bearing numbers/units that MUST still appear in the source (the check_data_claims lint compares digit-sequences+units under a loose match; a number change fails, a spelling change is fine; [] until the render pins them); `status` = final | preliminary | partial (the strength signal); `gloss` = a one-line description of the datum. THE ARGUMENTATIVE CHAIN (W-LEDGER 260803): every datum also carries `spine_claim` (or `spine_claims: []` when it genuinely bears weight for more than one) = the argument-spine claim id this number bears weight for (joins to book-models/argument_spine_declared.json — DL1); `observable` = the real-world quantity actually observed; `data_source` = how/where measured, with provenance (tool + method + artifact/commit); `limitation` = what the datum CANNOT show / the honest caveat. A preliminary datum with a stated limitation is honest; an unbound number is not. The extended check (DL1 join-integrity, DL2 four-fields-present, DL3 underquantified report, DL4 holds-still-appear) runs audit-only. The substantiation aggregator (`catalog.py substantiation`) joins these data-claims + the lit-positioning citations under each spine claim to flag under-substantiated-or-situated reality-claims. Regenerate the anchors + this file together when a source section moves. Queryable via `catalog.py data-claims`.

refactor-cost.observable: files touched + lines rewritten + wall-clock for one cross-format migration.
refactor-cost.data_source: An agent-run cross-format migration on the DocAble repo, measured from the landing commit's diffstat and the agent session's wall-clock log.
refactor-cost.limitation: One migration on one repo; wall-clock is agent time, not human-equivalent effort; not a controlled before/after against a hand-refactor baseline.
refactor-cost.gloss: A cross-format migration touched fifty-eight files and rewrote five thousand lines in about five hours of agent time — refactoring became an afternoon's work.

nearly-free.observable: Per-document remediation cost across three sources: do-it-yourself professor time, external-vendor per-page quote, and the tool's per-deck processing cost.
nearly-free.data_source: The DocAble cost model — measured per-deck processing cost (tokens + compute) set against published vendor per-page quotes and a DIY hours-per-document estimate (the book's canonical figures in metrics.json).
nearly-free.limitation: Cost-model estimates, not audited invoices; per-deck cost excludes amortized development; quality-parity with vendor output is asserted, not independently graded. `holds` stays empty by design: every figure in the reporting section is `{{token}}`-rendered from metrics.json (deck_issue_count, documents_per_course, hours_per_document, hours_per_course, workweeks_per_course, diy_cost_per_course, vendor_cost_per_page, vendor_cost_per_course_low/high) — the raw chapter source never carries a literal digit for the digit+unit pin to match, so pinning is delegated to the token registry (metrics.json) rather than to this ledger.
nearly-free.gloss: The per-document remediation cost cascade — do-it-yourself professor cost vs. external-vendor quote vs. the tool's per-deck processing cost — showing high-quality remediation nearly for free.

velocity.observable: Commits per week across the project's history. Loop-mode refinement (a ~2-week unattended autonomous-loop window): commits/day stayed FLAT (~176 -> 171) while durable throughput — the Epic-closure rate — rose, so a commits-per-week reading alone understates the mode's effect; velocity is not the productivity signal here.
velocity.data_source: A repo-activity histogram over the parent repo's git history (commits metric), 20 weeks from 2026-03-12 to 2026-07-29 (metrics.json _commit_provenance). The loop-mode flat-velocity reading is from a 28-day baseline vs 14-day loop-mode window re-verified at HEAD.
velocity.limitation: Commit count is a coarse activity proxy, not delivered value; the count mixes agent, human, and generated commits; single project, single fleet. Loop-mode caveat: commit counts include bookkeeping noise (squash / commit-slave / sentinel / tombstone commits), so the FLAT finding is robust but the absolute per-day number is not 'human-meaningful changes/day'; the window is ~2 weeks (one data point, not a trend). `holds` stays empty by design: the reporting section is a bare figure ([ref:velocity-curve]) with no digit-bearing prose sentence or caption in the chapter source, so there is no literal text for the digit+unit pin to match; the figure asset's own embedded description ("seven-week build") additionally reads as stale against the 20-week / commits_total=23,215 figures the token registry (metrics.json _commit_provenance) now carries, an asset-freshness gap outside this ledger's fix. Pinning would require either a chapter-text edit stating the axis-anchor values or a figure regeneration reconciling the two — an editorial call, not made here.
velocity.gloss: The velocity curve: commits per week across the project's history, rising as the fleet acquired capability then dipping during hardening.

mbse-nav-token.observable: Tokens-to-answer with MBSE navigation guidance ON versus OFF, across four modeled tasks.
mbse-nav-token.data_source: A controlled A/B pilot (N=4 modeled tasks); tokens-to-answer measured per task with guidance toggled, accuracy graded per answer.
mbse-nav-token.limitation: N=4 pilot — not powered; single fleet; measures tokens, not accuracy (zero accuracy loss noted, but at small N); the system-level Garden-null reframe of the MBSE ablation is coming in W5.
mbse-nav-token.gloss: A controlled A/B pilot of MBSE navigation guidance (N=4 modeled tasks): tokens-to-answer with guidance ON vs. OFF, 20% / 12% / 82% / 50% fewer tokens, median ~35% fewer, zero accuracy loss.

support-ratio-curve.observable: Support-apparatus source divided by production source at each week's last commit across 29 weeks: below parity in the prototype weeks, parity crossed around weeks 5-6, a steep climb through mechanization, then a plateau between roughly 3.5 and 3.9 across the mature era. Excluding documentation, tests dominate the support mass at about 1.75 million lines at the final week.
support-ratio-curve.data_source: A 29-week history-mining pass over the parent repo with its own category path-map, acquired 260925.103236; series in book/data/factory-archaeology-260925/loc_weekly.csv, the earlier authored snapshots in loc_snapshots.csv, write-up in book/data/factory-archaeology-260925/provenance/B_factory_capital.md. Supersedes the four-snapshot cloc curve (0.85 -> 2.48 -> 3.68 -> 3.06).
support-ratio-curve.limitation: LoC is a coarse proxy for effort. The weekly series is an INDEPENDENT re-derivation with its own category boundaries, not the earlier cloc configuration, so the levels are the mining pass's own and only the TREND (below parity, crosses, settles around three-to-one) is comparable across the two; the gap is left visible in the figure by overlaying the earlier snapshot ratios as diamonds. Only two of the four earlier snapshots carry a recoverable ratio, so only two diamonds render. Single repo, single-author fleet — a revealed preference, not a controlled comparison of governed vs. ungoverned development.
support-ratio-curve.gloss: The support ratio resolved weekly across 29 weeks: below parity in the prototype weeks, parity crossed around weeks 5-6, then a plateau between roughly 3.5 and 3.9 — the support apparatus outweighing the production source it exists to govern, several times over.

model-sync-efficacy.observable: The model-sync sensor's drift-detection readings and the reconciliation labor they drive: a derived-floor churn of +8,970 / -173 lines across 63 commits; 0 model-drift reopens across a separate, cumulative N=56 closes; and a first before-data report of ~27 findings at a signal-to-noise near 1.0.
model-sync-efficacy.data_source: The §3.8 model-sync measurement (draft committed f6147fc; the reporting section landed in W7). Figures from the sync report's churn ledger (63-commit refresh window) + the cumulative close ledger (N=56 closes, 0 reopens) + the first drift-detection report's finding tally.
model-sync-efficacy.limitation: A single subsystem's sync episode, before the drift-detector's signal-to-noise was tuned; the ~27-finding S:N~1.0 is a before-data snapshot, not a steady-state rate; not a controlled comparison against un-synced development. Primary binding is the drift-detection (alignment) claim; it also bears on the sync-cost-reduced (co-evolution economics) claim — see the parked-binding note in the results log.
model-sync-efficacy.gloss: The model-sync measurement: a drift-detection sensor whose readings (derived-floor churn +8,970/-173 lines across 63 commits; 0 model-drift reopens across a separate N=56 closes; ~27 pre-floor findings at S:N~1.0 before tuning) show reconciliation stays cheap and divergence is caught.

mmm-drain.observable: The Missing-Model-Metric orphan rate (share of tests whose exercised code reaches no model-anchored symbol) draining as subsystems get modeled across nine tracer re-runs: 56% -> 55% -> 52% -> 39% -> 32.2% -> 30.1% -> 20.9% -> 14.9% -> 7.89%.
mmm-drain.data_source: A code->model tracer (the MMM pilot tracer, trace.py) re-run over the dispatch/orchestration test population (~144-152 tests) after each model-loop Epic modeled the biggest remaining orphan cluster; sources in the missing-model-metric Epic docs + STRATEGY.
mmm-drain.limitation: The population denominator drifts 144->152 across runs, and the first (56%) point was subsystem-scoped — comparable, not a fixed-N series; the cost-rollup cluster's exact landing point is not separately enumerated. A fixed-N reproducible replay is parked (see results log). Render + holds pins land in W4.
mmm-drain.gloss: The Missing-Model-Metric drain: orphan (code-unmodelled) rate falling from 56% to 7.89% across nine tracer re-runs as the model-loop modeled each biggest orphan cluster in turn — code-to-model coverage rising to ~92%.

churn.observable: Per-path additions and deletions (web/ and backend/) across the four study windows; mechanization is the churn peak for both, then deletions collapse and later windows go net-additive (backend/ -286K deletions at mechanization -> -3.8K at hardening).
churn.data_source: git log --numstat scoped per path over the parent repo (2026-03-12 -> 2026-08-03), split into the four study-v2 commit-date windows (re-runnable commands in the w4-data scratchpad).
churn.limitation: Add/delete counts include generated, bundle, and vendored files — a churn/velocity signal, not hand-authored SLOC. A single-pass path partition now bounds that inflation: 0% on backend/, 14.6% of web/ additions (concentrated in the mechanization window at 24.5%, falling to 1-2% after the compiled output was git-ignored), 5.2% combined — so the curve is predominantly real source. Still a motion signal, not a clean measure of wasted rediscovery/undo/reconcile effort; single repo, single fleet.
churn.gloss: Path churn (web/ + backend/) across four windows: mechanization is the add-and-delete peak; later windows go net-additive as the built environment stabilizes the code.

control-growth.observable: Project-specific lint files, gate/check scripts and system-model files at each week's last commit across the project's 29 weeks: the lint-file count flat at zero through week 8, a sharp takeoff across weeks 9-11, then near-monotone stock-like growth to roughly 990 files at the mining head, with a weekly commits-to-lint-files correlation of approximately zero. Plus the failure-attribution discipline's footprint: 208 commits carrying a paired fix-and-lint tag and 27 lints naming the dated incident that motivated them.
control-growth.data_source: A 29-week history-mining pass over the parent repo (per-week last-commit tree scan), acquired 260925.103236; series in book/data/factory-archaeology-260925/control_growth_weekly.csv and cross_metric_correlations.csv, write-up in book/data/factory-archaeology-260925/provenance/C_governance_conversion.md. Supersedes the earlier four-snapshot curve (0 -> 336 -> 595 -> 747 lints; 0 -> 20 -> 76 -> 102 gates), one of whose points (595 at the hardening-window revision) the weekly series reproduces exactly and thereby validates the lint-file definition.
control-growth.limitation: A control-growth curve, not a causal rate: nothing in the record captures the failure-to-control edge, so the fraction of controls born from a failure rather than authored up front is not measured. Attribution is a documented, named discipline (208 paired fix-and-lint commits; 27 incident-citing lints), reported as such and not as a causal percentage. The gate-script and system-model companion traces use the mining pass's own definitions and are independent re-derivations, not reproductions of the earlier counts. Single repo, single fleet; counts are at the mining head (project week 29, 2026-09-21) and drift upward on re-run.
control-growth.gloss: The control substrate accumulating week by week across 29 weeks: lint files flat at zero through week 8, a sharp takeoff at weeks 9-11, then stock-like growth to roughly 990 — growth decoupled from that week's realization volume, which is what distinguishes deliberate investment from a side effect of throughput.

epic-closure-rate.observable: The Epic-closure rate — Epics moved into the closed set per week — across a 28-day baseline (19.3/wk) versus a 14-day unattended autonomous-loop-mode window (29.5/wk): a ~1.5x rise. The finishing / durable-throughput signal, distinct from raw commit velocity, which stayed flat over the same window.
epic-closure-rate.data_source: A per-week count of Epic directories moved into the closed set over a 28-day baseline vs a 14-day loop-mode window, re-verified at HEAD; the ~1.5x headline uses the rename+add counting rule.
epic-closure-rate.limitation: Epic-closure is method-sensitive; a briefed 2.3x did NOT reproduce. The verified range is ~1.3x-1.9x depending on the counting rule (rename-only 1.29x / rename+add 1.53x headline / any-touch 1.92x, which over-counts appended fix-ups); every measure agrees on DIRECTION, so headline the ~1.5x and state the band. The window is ~2 weeks — one data point, not a trend. Single repo, single fleet. `holds` stays empty by design: the datum is registered in the ledger ahead of its chapter render (no digit-bearing prose sentence exists yet in 5.2 for a digit+unit pin to match); the render + holds pins land with the loop-mode 5.2 write-up. Bound to the H2 theory hypothesis (governance moderation) as preliminary supporting data — flat velocity beside a rising closure rate is the anti-decay shape H2 predicts, offered for replication, not proven.
epic-closure-rate.gloss: The Epic-closure rate rising ~1.5x (baseline 19.3/wk -> loop-mode 29.5/wk; band 1.3x-1.9x by counting rule) — the finishing / durable-throughput signal that rose while raw commit velocity stayed flat, the anti-decay shape a high-quality governed environment predicts.
